values: to notice
to become aware of
S’apercevoir de takes a noun or pronoun and means to notice or become aware of something.
S’apercevoir que introduces a complete clause stating what the subject realizes or notices.
Requires à before a noun and à ce que + subjunctive before a clause; with an infinitive, the subject normally expects to perform the action.
With a plural subject, the pronominal form is normally reciprocal and means that the participants kiss one another.
to take possession of
to take control of
The verb is used only pronominally in this sense and requires de before the thing seized.
The pronouns se and en are integral to the expression; in the imperative, use va-t’en and allez-vous-en.
S’ennuyer means to be bored; s’ennuyer de quelqu’un or de quelque chose can mean to miss them, especially in Canadian French.
S’entendre avec describes having a good or workable relationship with someone; bien or mal can specify the quality of the relationship.
Can describe literal flight or a sudden disappearance, and figuratively a rapid increase in prices or figures.
Takes à before a noun or infinitive and describes the process of becoming accustomed, unlike être habitué à, which often describes the resulting state.
to deal with
to be in charge of
Depending on context, s’occuper de means to care for, handle, or take responsibility for someone or something.
The indirect reflexive pronoun means for oneself; the thing obtained remains the direct object.
With a plural subject this is reciprocal: the participants write to one another; the pronoun is indirect, so the past participle normally does not agree with it.
Sans que requires the subjunctive and is used when the subordinate clause has its own subject; with the same subject, use sans + infinitive.
Savoir + infinitive expresses learned knowledge or knowing how to perform an action; pouvoir emphasizes ability or possibility instead.
Introduces an indirect yes-or-no question; si here means whether, not a condition.

batch_summary: Added high-value complementation and reciprocity notes for pronominal verbs and clarified the use of sans que, savoir + infinitive, and savoir si.
